# Xenon map: who does what

<!-- Written by `npm run map` from tools/map/features.json. Do not edit this file by hand: -->
<!-- change features.json and run the command. A test fails when the two disagree. -->

Xenon is four pieces that talk to each other:

- **The engine** (`server/`, Node.js): a small local web server on `127.0.0.1:3030`. It reads the PC, runs actions and keeps the data.
- **The screen** (`server/index.html`, `server/js/`, `server/components/`, `server/styles/`): the dashboard, a web page the engine serves. A phone opens the same page.
- **The app** (`apps/native/`, Rust + Tauri): the window that shows the screen, starts the engine and draws widgets over the desktop.
- **The helpers** (`helper/` in C#, `helper-mac/` in Swift): small programs for the things only the operating system can do.

Below, every feature has one line saying what it does and where its files are. A file belongs to the first feature that names it.

The program behind everything: it starts, answers the screen, saves settings, updates itself.

## App and helpers

The native programs around the engine, and the code that differs per operating system.

| Feature | What it does | Where |

| **Helper for Windows** | A small C# program for media, windows, audio levels and the file index. | `helper/**` |
| **Helper for macOS** | The same helper in Swift, speaking the same protocol. | `helper-mac/**` |

## Keeping this map true

- A new file that fits an existing pattern needs nothing.
- A new file that fits none: add its path to the right feature in `tools/map/features.json`, then run `npm run map`.
- A new feature: add an entry (name, one line on what it does, its files), then run `npm run map`.
- `npm test` fails when a file has no owner, a pattern points at nothing, or this page is out of date.
